analyst_view.overall: Early view: Besiktas's home game is due to be played in Batumi, Georgia, on security grounds (one Turkish report says their fans will be let in), which takes away some of the Istanbul edge. Vincenzo Italiano's side are 8th with 7 points but have conceded in all four league-phase games, while Israeli champions Hapoel Beer Sheva are 33rd and have scored once in four.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.8 goals. I lean slightly higher: all four Besiktas games in this league phase have had four or five goals (11 scored, 8 conceded), and Orkun Kokcu, back from a foot injury, scored at Celtic. Hapoel have one goal in four, so most of the goals should come at one end, but Besiktas's habit of conceding keeps a 3-1 type score in play.

corners.text: The numbers say 7.1 corners, which looks low for a game in which the site expects Besiktas to take 18 shots. They should have most of the ball against a side that has failed to score in three straight games, and with Leandro Trossard among their attackers they should force plenty of blocks and corners, so I'd expect 8 or 9.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.5 cards. I lean a little higher: the game was moved out of Turkey on security grounds, which makes for a tense backdrop, and a bottom-four side still chasing its first win tends to foul more as the game wears on. The referee has not been named.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.4 shots, 18.4 of them from Besiktas. That fits how their European games have gone, with chances at both ends. The neutral venue may take a little off Besiktas's home pressure, while Hapoel's 7.9 looks generous, so the two roughly cancel out.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.7 shots on target, a high figure. Hapoel's attack has barely tested anyone in this league phase (no goals in their last three, including 0-2 at home to OFI), so three on target from them looks generous, and I'd expect 9 or 10 in total.
